skill.name: qa-check
skill.description: Run pre-pull-request quality checks for backend and frontend code. The workflow covers Gradle checks, pnpm lint, tests, builds, coverage thresholds, and a clear QA report.
skill.summary: Run lint, tests, builds, and coverage checks before opening a pull request.

security_audit.summary: The skill is a project-specific QA checklist that documents Gradle and pnpm validation commands. All static findings were false positives from Markdown backticks, benign /dev/null redirection, or a heuristic entropy signal; no prompt injection, exfiltration, or destructive workflow was found.

remediation.issue: Hardcoded local project path in instructions
remediation.suggestion: Replace the absolute /Users path with a workspace-relative project-root check before marketplace publication.

remediation.issue: Command execution boundaries are not explicit
remediation.suggestion: State that QA commands should run only inside the active repository and after normal user approval for local command execution.

content.user_title: Run QA Checks Before Pull Requests
content.value_statement: Teams need fast PR checks before code review. This skill runs a clear QA workflow for backend and frontend validation.
actual_capabilities: Runs backend Gradle checks and JaCoCo coverage verification when requested.
Runs frontend lint, build, and coverage commands through pnpm filters.
Checks project root prerequisites before backend or frontend validation.
Compares coverage and lint results against documented thresholds.
Produces a pass, fail, or warning QA report with next steps.
limitations: Designed around a specific MovieMarketer or YouTubeOpsAI project layout.
Depends on local Gradle, pnpm, frontend, and backend setup.
Cannot prove coverage if reports or commands are unavailable.
Does not replace human review of product behavior or requirements.

use_cases.title: Backend readiness check
use_cases.description: Validate Gradle checks and coverage before asking for backend code review.

use_cases.title: Frontend PR validation
use_cases.description: Run lint, build, and coverage checks for frontend changes before opening a PR.

use_cases.title: Release quality gate
use_cases.description: Review combined backend and frontend status before approving release branches.

prompt_templates.title: Run the default QA check
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a quick full-stack validation before a PR.

prompt_templates.title: Check only the frontend
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when only frontend files changed.

prompt_templates.title: Check backend without coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a faster backend check when coverage is not required.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a failed QA gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Run qa-check for both targets, include coverage, and list each failing command with the recommended fix order.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when a branch fails readiness checks and needs triage.

output_examples.input: Run a full QA check before opening a pull request.
output_examples.output: Overall result: failed. Backend checks passed. Frontend build failed on type errors. Next steps: fix type errors, rerun build, then rerun full QA.

output_examples.input: Run a frontend-only check with coverage enabled.
output_examples.output: Overall result: warning. Lint and build passed. Coverage is below the target. Next steps: add tests for low-coverage UI logic.

output_examples.input: Run a backend check without coverage.
output_examples.output: Overall result: passed with coverage skipped. Gradle checks passed. Next steps: run coverage before final review if the team requires it.

best_practices: Run the skill from the intended project root.
Keep coverage enabled for final PR readiness checks.
Review failed command logs before applying fixes.
anti_patterns: Do not treat skipped coverage as final approval.
Do not run the workflow in unrelated repository layouts.
Do not ignore failed lint, test, or build steps.

faq.question: What does this skill check?
faq.answer: It checks backend Gradle quality tasks, frontend lint, frontend build, tests, coverage, and a final QA status.

faq.question: Can I run only frontend checks?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the frontend target when backend files did not change.

faq.question: Can I run only backend checks?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the backend target, with optional coverage skipping for faster local checks.

faq.question: Does it fix code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It reports failures and suggests next steps for the developer to apply.

faq.question: Does it require local tools?
faq.answer: Yes. The repository must have the expected Gradle, pnpm, frontend, and backend setup.

faq.question: Is it a replacement for CI?
faq.answer: No. It is a local readiness check that should complement CI and code review.
